text:
maria: Heads-up: acme-inc (dedicated pool d-42) reporting a 3x drop in throughput since ~02:03 UTC. Tokens/sec down, tail latency up. No 5xxs in API gateway. Can someone triage?

alex: looking. any recent deploys or config changes to batcher/scheduler?

maria: nothing on app side. They started seeing it right after autoscale event at 02:01. I filed initial support ticket: https://redwood/support/INC-8159

ops-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-d-42.autoscaler scaled down from 12 -> 6 at 02:01 (policy: idle reclaim).

john: I see a spike in micro-batch counts and more thin batches in the continuous-batcher metrics around 02:00-02:10. Prefill latency increased too.

kira: we shipped a packing heuristic tweak yesterday (PR #4721) that changes max_batch_tokens default from 4096 -> 8192 for long sequences. Could be interaction with small request sizes causing poor packing.

alex: interesting. If max_batch_tokens doubled, small requests might create more fragmentation. Can we confirm per-tenant batch size distribution for d-42?

john: pulling metrics: avg batch tokens dropped from 2800 -> 1400, avg batch occupancy dropped ~45%. Batch count per second rose 2.8x. That matches throughput drop.

maria: customer logs show client is sending many 256-token requests. Previously they got merged into big batches; now they're landing in separate microbatches.

kira: can someone try reverting the packing heuristic in canary or temp-change max_batch_tokens back to 4096 on d-42? Quick mitigation: force max_batch_tokens=4096 and restart batcher worker to re-align scheduling.

sre-oncall: on it. Running emergency config change on d-42: 
```
# temporary override
batcher.max_batch_tokens=4096
batcher.scheduler.quantum_ms=6
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: config override applied to pool d-42 at 02:28 UTC. No restart required.

john: metrics: batch occupancy improving within 30s. avg tokens per batch climbing back to ~2600. Throughput trending up.

maria: acme-inc confirms latency dropping in their traces. They reported 80% improvement on recent requests. :thumbsup:

sam-support: notified customer of mitigation and that engineering is investigating root cause.

kira: follow-up: PR #4721 had a side-effect where the scheduler's quantum wasn't adjusted for the new token cap; that created more, smaller scheduling windows. We should revert the heuristic until we add a quantum-adaptive step.

alex: filing a postmortem and rollback plan. Action items: 1) revert packing change or add adaptive quantum in PR, 2) add per-pool canary for packing heuristics, 3) add alert if batch occupancy drops >30% vs baseline.

maria: thanks all. We'll keep d-42 at forced 4096 until change is merged. Closing loop with acme-inc after postmortem.

sre-oncall: marking incident resolved for now; will reopen if regression returns. Incident ref: INC-8159.
